title: Ironically, this developer lost focus
body:
This used to be a fairly decent app, but after many years of use of this app, and the old app from this developer, I will now stop using this app. It is just getting worse and worse with every update, while issues are not being fixed.

My biggest gripes :
- The UI is more and more getting bloated with new features that are not needed by me, but that are pushed to the front in an effort to monetise the app.
- Meanwhile a feature that is vital for the pomodoro technique is moved to a sub-menu, when it used to be front and center.
- The app now frequently asks for feedback, just when I start a focus timer. Rarely the developers response to the feedback. What an extremely weird moment to ask for feedback, when the user just starts a focus session.
-  When the app is run in the background the app shows live activity information about the timer in the top of the screen, and on the lock screen, showing information about the timer. This is a big plus compared to similar focus apps. However, it gives outdated information once a focus session has ended and a new one (or a break) has been started automatically. I've reported this multiple times, but the app developer seems unable to fix this, so I have to get used to reading incorrect information.
- The same applies to the widget that can be added to the home screen. It shows information about the number of focus rounds I did, but most of the time it shows outdated information, and I need to manually open the app to update the information. It defeats the purpose of a widget. Instead of fixing this the developers have 'fixed' this by now sometimes just showing a refresh button that opens the app. How other apps are able to show updated information in their widgets and this app seemingly not is beyond me.
- While the app seems to be designed to be able to run in the background, if I actually do that the app classifies this as me being distracted during a focus session, and bugs me with a popup about it, hoping to sell the Focus Shield feature I don't need. The developers should not pretent to know if me using another app while in a focus session is related to the focus session or me actually being distracted. But they do, just to use it in order to try to sell.
- When the app is run it the background it not always sounds an alarm when the timer has ended, while this is the most important feature of any focus timer app. It happens rarely, but it does happen.
- I wanted to switch back to the old free version, but the developer removed that version from the store.

title: Add “edit, delete, or adjust” options
body: The app is very nice, but it happened to me twice that I forgot to stop the timer and it counted me 22h of work. I can’t delete or edit it, which affects my weekly statistics and adds the work that I haven’t done. Also, if you forget to mark your habit as „done”, everything for the previous day gets blocked the next day. Having adhd means you often forget things, so it would be helpful to be able to edit the previous day or adjust the extra time added to your focus session.
